22	# TL;DR
23	
24	Outcome: Dock Home moves to a relay-owned, provider-agnostic session-table stream. Each configured relay host sends a full `hosts[]` + `sessions[]` snapshot first, then ordered deltas, and the iPhone only applies snapshots/deltas, resyncs on gaps, unions normalized tables, and renders.
25	
26	Problem: today's client calls raw Codex-shaped `thread/list`, fans out across hosts and scopes, decodes provider status/source fields, and publishes destructive partial snapshots. Slow Home refreshes can temporarily show zero Home rows, and Codex `notLoaded` leaks into the product as a confusing visible row status.
27	
28	Approach: make the relay the stateful aggregator for each host. The relay owns provider adapters, live/history merge, status normalization, last-good atomic JSON persistence, stale-while-refresh semantics, and the clean `dock/*` wire protocol. The client does not decode Codex list rows or runtime concepts.
29	
30	Plan: build the protocol, relay session table, last-good persistence, and fake-provider proof first; add the Codex adapter; add the Swift stream client/reducer; cut Dock Home over; prove the behavior in simulator; delete the old Home list path; then run physical-device and docs cleanup.
31	
32	Non-negotiables: no raw `notLoaded` on the Dock Home wire; no destructive row clearing on slow or failed refresh; no provider-specific source/status decoding in the client; no runtime shims or permanent dual Home paths; simulator proof is primary client completion evidence.

104	# 0) Holistic North Star
105	
106	## 0.1 The claim (falsifiable)
107	
108	After this plan is implemented, Dock Home will no longer call raw `thread/list`
109	for its primary list, will no longer expose raw Codex `notLoaded` as a row
110	status, and will retain last-known rows when a relay host is slow, stale,
111	offline, or restarting. A simulator run with a scripted fake relay must prove
112	that selected Home rows do not drop to zero during a slow/stale refresh while
113	another host continues updating.
114	
115	## 0.2 In scope
116	
117	- New relay-owned `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, and `dock/resync` contract.
118	- Per-host relay `SessionTable` with `epoch`, `seq`, `asOf`, freshness, host
119	  metadata, and normalized session rows.
120	- Relay `SyncLoop` that polls provider adapters, merges base/history rows with
121	  live runtime state, normalizes status/lane/source, diffs rows, and emits
122	  ordered deltas.
123	- Last-good normalized table persistence using atomic JSON under `.codex-dock/`.
124	- Codex provider adapter built from current relay pieces.
125	- Swift Dock Home stream client, reducer/table store, and mapping into existing
126	  Dock presentation.
127	- Deleting or retiring old Dock Home raw `thread/list`, scope fan-out,
128	  dedupe/conflict, `liveOverlay`, and `notLoaded` product-state paths once the
129	  new path is simulator-proven.
130	- Scripted fake relay/simulator hooks needed to prove slow/stale/resync behavior
131	  deterministically.
132	- Relay and Swift tests that protect the new provider-agnostic wire contract.
133	- Preserving existing raw detail/control/archive/voice and other non-Home
134	  flows as explicit non-Home contracts for this plan.
135	
136	## 0.3 Out of scope
137	
138	- Implementing the plan in this planning pass.
139	- Building a coordinator/federation relay in V1.
140	- Adding Claude Code support in V1; the adapter boundary must allow it later.
141	- SQLite, persistent event sourcing, CRDTs, message buses, or cross-reconnect
142	  delta replay logs.
143	- Renaming all existing `thread/*` methods to `session/*` now.
144	- Reworking the entire thread detail/event UI.
145	- Replacing physical device testing with unit tests.
146	- Introducing runtime fallbacks that keep two permanent Dock Home data paths.
147	
148	## 0.4 Definition of done (acceptance evidence)
149	
150	- Relay tests pass with `rtk npm run test:relay`.
151	- Swift contract tests pass for the new stream DTO/reducer path with the
152	  smallest relevant `rtk swift test --filter ...` command once concrete test
153	  ownership exists.
154	- Generated-project simulator tests run with `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'`.
155	- The app launches with `rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'`.
156	- Simulator logs from `rtk make sim-logs SIM='iPhone 17'` show:
157	  - Dock Home subscribing through `dock/subscribe`.
158	  - Full snapshot application.
159	  - Ordered delta application.
160	  - Resync after a forced sequence gap.
161	  - Rows retained while a host is stale or reconnecting.
162	  - No Dock Home raw `thread/list` paging path.
163	- A scripted fake relay proves the slow Home case deterministically.
164	- Physical install path is exercised with `rtk make iphone-17-pro` when the
165	  simulator path is green and signing/device state allow it.
166	
167	## 0.5 Key invariants (fix immediately if violated)
168	
169	- `notLoaded` is an adapter input only; it is not a valid Dock Home wire status.
170	- Host connection, table freshness, and row runtime status stay separate.
171	- Failed or slow sync never clears last-known rows.
172	- `dock/update` deltas are applied only when `epoch` matches and `baseSeq`
173	  equals the client's current `seq`; otherwise the client resyncs.
174	- The relay persists normalized last-good state only, not raw provider payloads
175	  or secrets.
176	- Phone-side configuration remains host/port bootstrap and relay auth only.
177	- No OpenAI keys, raw app-server bearer tokens, loopback URLs, or
178	  `dockRelaySource` values cross the phone wire.
179	- New timeouts, intervals, ports, page sizes, and caps belong in existing
180	  constants files, not scattered literals.
181	- Makefile-owned commands remain the mobile build/install source of truth.

183	# 1) Key Design Considerations (what matters most)
184	
185	## 1.1 Priorities (ranked)
186	
187	1. Stable user experience under slow, stale, offline, reconnecting, and restart
188	   states.
189	2. Clean provider-agnostic client contract.
190	3. Relay ownership of provider complexity, freshness, retry/backoff, and
191	   last-good state.
192	4. Deterministic simulator proof for the slow/stale/resync cases.
193	5. Minimal topology: per-host relays in V1, coordinator deferred.
194	6. Delete superseded Home complexity after the new path is proven.
195	7. Preserve existing non-Home raw detail/control/archive/voice behavior until
196	   those flows have their own migration plan.
197	
198	## 1.2 Constraints
199	
200	- The app normally connects to the Dock relay on `:4510`, not raw app-server
201	  `:4500`.
202	- The repo's canonical commands are in `Makefile`, `Package.swift`,
203	  `package.json`, and `project.yml`.
204	- Mobile builds and installs must use `rtk make ...` targets.
205	- Relay changes under `scripts/dock-relay*.mjs` start with
206	  `rtk npm run test:relay`.
207	- Installed UI behavior requires simulator or physical-device evidence; unit
208	  tests alone do not prove the user experience.
209	- Physical iPhone configuration stays per-device and host/port based.
210	- Secrets stay relay-side.
211	- Runtime shims and fallbacks are forbidden unless explicitly approved and
212	  timeboxed; no such approval exists for this plan.
213	
214	## 1.3 Architectural principles (rules we will enforce)
215	
216	- Use one canonical Dock Home data contract: `dock/*` snapshots/deltas.
217	- Keep provider adapters behind the relay boundary.
218	- Keep the client reducer mechanical: snapshot replace, delta apply, resync on
219	  gap.
220	- Represent freshness explicitly instead of implying it through row presence.
221	- Delete or retire old Home code paths when the new path is proven.
222	- Reuse existing relay logging and constants modules.
223	- Reuse existing app logging under subsystem `com.aelaguiz.CodexDock`.
224	- Add comments only at sharp contract boundaries: sequence/gap semantics,
225	  persisted-table schema, and provider adapter normalization.
226	
227	## 1.4 Known tradeoffs (explicit)
228	
229	- Push subscription is more work than polling a cached snapshot, but it directly
230	  satisfies the incremental update and precise staleness requirement.
231	- Per-host streams mean the client keeps multiple sockets, but the union is only
232	  normalized UI composition, not raw provider merge logic.
233	- Atomic JSON persistence is less flexible than SQLite, but it is enough for V1
234	  and avoids a database migration before the behavior is proven.
235	- Preserving existing non-Home raw detail/control/archive/voice APIs is an
236	  explicit compatibility boundary for this plan, not a Dock Home fallback;
237	  future migration requires a separate plan.
238	
239	# 2) Problem Statement (existing architecture + why change)
240	
241	## 2.1 What exists today
242	
243	Dock Home loads rows by asking each configured relay for Codex-shaped
244	`thread/list` data. The Swift client runs active human and active agent scopes,
245	pages cursors, maps `ThreadListDTO` into `SessionSummary`, deduplicates scoped
246	rows, builds `DockSnapshot`, and publishes partial snapshots while other hosts
247	are still checking.
248	
249	The relay is in the path, but for `thread/list` it still reads history on the
250	request path, warms a summary cache, and attaches a `liveOverlay` rather than
251	owning a durable provider-agnostic Dock table.
252	
253	## 2.2 What's broken / missing (concrete)
254	
255	- Slow Home refreshes can temporarily produce a selected-host view with zero
256	  rows because Home has not completed the current refresh yet.
257	- `notLoaded` is visible as a Dock row status even though it is a Codex runtime
258	  memory detail.
259	- The client must understand Codex status, source kind, agent-vs-human
260	  classification, cursor paging, `liveOverlay`, and partial failures.
261	- Future Claude Code support would require Swift changes if the client keeps
262	  decoding provider-specific list rows.
263	- The current tests lock in some wrong product contracts, especially "history
264	  status wins" for list rows.
265	
266	## 2.3 Constraints implied by the problem
267	
268	- The relay must serve warm state quickly and refresh in the background.
269	- Failed refresh must become stale metadata, not an empty list.
270	- The new contract must be provider-agnostic before the client adopts it.
271	- The old Home path must be deleted or disabled after cutover, or the app will
272	  keep two sources of truth.
273	- The slow Home case must be forceable in simulator; relying on real network
274	  timing is not good enough.

282	  renders last-known-good data while freshness updates separately. Reject using
283	  browser-style polling as the primary mechanism because this product needs
284	  incremental updates and explicit resync.
285	- Sequence-based replication contracts - adopt `epoch`, `seq`, `baseSeq`, and

287	  Reject durable event-sourcing in V1 because the working set is a few hosts and
288	  hundreds of rows, not a distributed database.
289	- Provider adapter boundary - adopt the adapter pattern for Codex now and

405	# 4) Current Architecture (as-is)
406	
407	<!-- arch_skill:block:current_architecture:start -->
408	## 4.1 On-disk structure
409	
410	- Relay code lives in `scripts/dock-relay*.mjs`.
411	- Current list aggregation lives mostly in `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`.
412	- Current live status polling lives in `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs`.
413	- Swift app-server DTOs and JSON-RPC transport live in `CodexDock/AppServer/`.
414	- Dock Home state and projection live in `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`,
415	  `DockSessionProjection.swift`, and `SessionRowProjector.swift`.
416	- Dock Home views live under `CodexDock/Features/Dock/`.
417	
418	## 4.2 Control paths (runtime)
419	
420	Current Dock Home flow:
421	
422	```text
423	DockView / AppLifecycle -> DockStore.reload
424	  -> loadAllHostsPublishingPartial
425	  -> per host, per scope AppServerDockClient.loadSessions
426	  -> relay thread/list
427	  -> history app-server thread/list
428	  -> Swift SessionSummaryMapper
429	  -> DockStore.makeSnapshot
430	  -> DockSessionProjection
431	  -> Dock views
432	```
433	
434	The relay's current `thread/list` path is request-time aggregation, not a
435	durable Dock-state stream.
436	
437	## 4.3 Object model + key abstractions
438	
439	- `ThreadListDTO` is Codex-shaped.
440	- `SessionSummary` is Swift's current mapped row model.
441	- `DockRowViewModel` is the current presentation row.
442	- `DockSnapshot` is built by Swift from the currently completed host/scope
443	  results.
444	- `ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO` reports live status metadata but does not replace
445	  the row status.
446	- `DockRowStatusKind.notLoaded` is a user-visible row status today.
447	
448	## 4.4 Observability + failure behavior today
449

# TL;DR

Outcome: Dock Home moves to a relay-owned, provider-agnostic session-table stream. Each configured relay host sends a full `hosts[]` + `sessions[]` snapshot first, then ordered deltas, and the iPhone only applies snapshots/deltas, resyncs on gaps, unions normalized tables, and renders.

Problem: today's client calls raw Codex-shaped `thread/list`, fans out across hosts and scopes, decodes provider status/source fields, and publishes destructive partial snapshots. Slow Home refreshes can temporarily show zero Home rows, and Codex `notLoaded` leaks into the product as a confusing visible row status.

Approach: make the relay the stateful aggregator for each host. The relay owns provider adapters, live/history merge, status normalization, last-good atomic JSON persistence, stale-while-refresh semantics, and the clean `dock/*` wire protocol. The client does not decode Codex list rows or runtime concepts.

Plan: build the protocol, relay session table, last-good persistence, and fake-provider proof first; add the Codex adapter; add the Swift stream client/reducer; cut Dock Home over; prove the behavior in simulator; delete the old Home list path; then run physical-device and docs cleanup.

Non-negotiables: no raw `notLoaded` on the Dock Home wire; no destructive row clearing on slow or failed refresh; no provider-specific source/status decoding in the client; no runtime shims or permanent dual Home paths; simulator proof is primary client completion evidence.

# 0) Holistic North Star

## 0.1 The claim (falsifiable)

After this plan is implemented, Dock Home will no longer call raw `thread/list`
for its primary list, will no longer expose raw Codex `notLoaded` as a row
status, and will retain last-known rows when a relay host is slow, stale,
offline, or restarting. A simulator run with a scripted fake relay must prove
that selected Home rows do not drop to zero during a slow/stale refresh while
another host continues updating.

## 0.2 In scope

- New relay-owned `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, and `dock/resync` contract.
- Per-host relay `SessionTable` with `epoch`, `seq`, `asOf`, freshness, host
  metadata, and normalized session rows.
- Relay `SyncLoop` that polls provider adapters, merges base/history rows with
  live runtime state, normalizes status/lane/source, diffs rows, and emits
  ordered deltas.
- Last-good normalized table persistence using atomic JSON under `.codex-dock/`.
- Codex provider adapter built from current relay pieces.
- Swift Dock Home stream client, reducer/table store, and mapping into existing
  Dock presentation.
- Deleting or retiring old Dock Home raw `thread/list`, scope fan-out,
  dedupe/conflict, `liveOverlay`, and `notLoaded` product-state paths once the
  new path is simulator-proven.
- Scripted fake relay/simulator hooks needed to prove slow/stale/resync behavior
  deterministically.
- Relay and Swift tests that protect the new provider-agnostic wire contract.
- Preserving existing raw detail/control/archive/voice and other non-Home
  flows as explicit non-Home contracts for this plan.

## 0.3 Out of scope

- Implementing the plan in this planning pass.
- Building a coordinator/federation relay in V1.
- Adding Claude Code support in V1; the adapter boundary must allow it later.
- SQLite, persistent event sourcing, CRDTs, message buses, or cross-reconnect
  delta replay logs.
- Renaming all existing `thread/*` methods to `session/*` now.
- Reworking the entire thread detail/event UI.
- Replacing physical device testing with unit tests.
- Introducing runtime fallbacks that keep two permanent Dock Home data paths.

## 0.4 Definition of done (acceptance evidence)

- Relay tests pass with `rtk npm run test:relay`.
- Swift contract tests pass for the new stream DTO/reducer path with the
  smallest relevant `rtk swift test --filter ...` command once concrete test
  ownership exists.
- Generated-project simulator tests run with `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'`.
- The app launches with `rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'`.
- Simulator logs from `rtk make sim-logs SIM='iPhone 17'` show:
  - Dock Home subscribing through `dock/subscribe`.
  - Full snapshot application.
  - Ordered delta application.
  - Resync after a forced sequence gap.
  - Rows retained while a host is stale or reconnecting.
  - No Dock Home raw `thread/list` paging path.
- A scripted fake relay proves the slow Home case deterministically.
- Physical install path is exercised with `rtk make iphone-17-pro` when the
  simulator path is green and signing/device state allow it.

## 0.5 Key invariants (fix immediately if violated)

- `notLoaded` is an adapter input only; it is not a valid Dock Home wire status.
- Host connection, table freshness, and row runtime status stay separate.
- Failed or slow sync never clears last-known rows.
- `dock/update` deltas are applied only when `epoch` matches and `baseSeq`
  equals the client's current `seq`; otherwise the client resyncs.
- The relay persists normalized last-good state only, not raw provider payloads
  or secrets.
- Phone-side configuration remains host/port bootstrap and relay auth only.
- No OpenAI keys, raw app-server bearer tokens, loopback URLs, or
  `dockRelaySource` values cross the phone wire.
- New timeouts, intervals, ports, page sizes, and caps belong in existing
  constants files, not scattered literals.
- Makefile-owned commands remain the mobile build/install source of truth.

# 1) Key Design Considerations (what matters most)

## 1.1 Priorities (ranked)

1. Stable user experience under slow, stale, offline, reconnecting, and restart
   states.
2. Clean provider-agnostic client contract.
3. Relay ownership of provider complexity, freshness, retry/backoff, and
   last-good state.
4. Deterministic simulator proof for the slow/stale/resync cases.
5. Minimal topology: per-host relays in V1, coordinator deferred.
6. Delete superseded Home complexity after the new path is proven.
7. Preserve existing non-Home raw detail/control/archive/voice behavior until
   those flows have their own migration plan.

## 1.2 Constraints

- The app normally connects to the Dock relay on `:4510`, not raw app-server
  `:4500`.
- The repo's canonical commands are in `Makefile`, `Package.swift`,
  `package.json`, and `project.yml`.
- Mobile builds and installs must use `rtk make ...` targets.
- Relay changes under `scripts/dock-relay*.mjs` start with
  `rtk npm run test:relay`.
- Installed UI behavior requires simulator or physical-device evidence; unit
  tests alone do not prove the user experience.
- Physical iPhone configuration stays per-device and host/port based.
- Secrets stay relay-side.
- Runtime shims and fallbacks are forbidden unless explicitly approved and
  timeboxed; no such approval exists for this plan.

## 1.3 Architectural principles (rules we will enforce)

- Use one canonical Dock Home data contract: `dock/*` snapshots/deltas.
- Keep provider adapters behind the relay boundary.
- Keep the client reducer mechanical: snapshot replace, delta apply, resync on
  gap.
- Represent freshness explicitly instead of implying it through row presence.
- Delete or retire old Home code paths when the new path is proven.
- Reuse existing relay logging and constants modules.
- Reuse existing app logging under subsystem `com.aelaguiz.CodexDock`.
- Add comments only at sharp contract boundaries: sequence/gap semantics,
  persisted-table schema, and provider adapter normalization.

## 1.4 Known tradeoffs (explicit)

- Push subscription is more work than polling a cached snapshot, but it directly
  satisfies the incremental update and precise staleness requirement.
- Per-host streams mean the client keeps multiple sockets, but the union is only
  normalized UI composition, not raw provider merge logic.
- Atomic JSON persistence is less flexible than SQLite, but it is enough for V1
  and avoids a database migration before the behavior is proven.
- Preserving existing non-Home raw detail/control/archive/voice APIs is an
  explicit compatibility boundary for this plan, not a Dock Home fallback;
  future migration requires a separate plan.

# 2) Problem Statement (existing architecture + why change)

## 2.1 What exists today

Dock Home loads rows by asking each configured relay for Codex-shaped
`thread/list` data. The Swift client runs active human and active agent scopes,
pages cursors, maps `ThreadListDTO` into `SessionSummary`, deduplicates scoped
rows, builds `DockSnapshot`, and publishes partial snapshots while other hosts
are still checking.

The relay is in the path, but for `thread/list` it still reads history on the
request path, warms a summary cache, and attaches a `liveOverlay` rather than
owning a durable provider-agnostic Dock table.

## 2.2 What's broken / missing (concrete)

- Slow Home refreshes can temporarily produce a selected-host view with zero
  rows because Home has not completed the current refresh yet.
- `notLoaded` is visible as a Dock row status even though it is a Codex runtime
  memory detail.
- The client must understand Codex status, source kind, agent-vs-human
  classification, cursor paging, `liveOverlay`, and partial failures.
- Future Claude Code support would require Swift changes if the client keeps
  decoding provider-specific list rows.
- The current tests lock in some wrong product contracts, especially "history
  status wins" for list rows.

## 2.3 Constraints implied by the problem

- The relay must serve warm state quickly and refresh in the background.
- Failed refresh must become stale metadata, not an empty list.
- The new contract must be provider-agnostic before the client adopts it.
- The old Home path must be deleted or disabled after cutover, or the app will
  keep two sources of truth.
- The slow Home case must be forceable in simulator; relying on real network
  timing is not good enough.

# 3) Research Grounding (external + internal "ground truth")

<!-- arch_skill:block:research_grounding:start -->
## 3.1 External anchors (papers, systems, prior art)

- Local-first stale-while-refresh UI pattern - adopt the core idea that the UI
  renders last-known-good data while freshness updates separately. Reject using
  browser-style polling as the primary mechanism because this product needs
  incremental updates and explicit resync.
- Sequence-based replication contracts - adopt `epoch`, `seq`, `baseSeq`, and
  full-snapshot resync because they are easy to test and make gaps fail loud.

## 5.3 Object model + abstractions (future)

Relay:

- `SessionTable` owns `schemaVersion`, `epoch`, `seq`, `asOf`, `freshness`,
  `hosts`, `sessions`, and `lastError`.
- `ProviderAdapter` hides provider-specific list/live/detail/control behavior.
- `CodexAdapter` converts Codex history/live/runtime facts into normalized
  sessions.
- `SubscriberRegistry` sends snapshots/deltas and coalesces slow subscribers.
- `DockProtocol` serializes provider-agnostic `dock/*` messages.
- `LastGoodStore` atomically persists normalized table JSON.

Wire protocol:

```text
dock/subscribe -> snapshot { schemaVersion, epoch, seq, asOf, freshness, hosts[], sessions[] }
dock/update    -> delta { epoch, baseSeq, seq, upsertHosts[], upsertSessions[], deleteSessionIDs[] }
dock/update    -> heartbeat { epoch, seq, asOf, freshness }
dock/resync    -> full snapshot
```

- `dock/subscribe` is a client request. The first full snapshot is the
  `dock/subscribe` response.
- `dock/update` is a server-to-client notification only. Delta updates include
  `baseSeq`; heartbeat updates do not include `baseSeq`.
- `dock/resync` is a client request that returns a full snapshot.
- WebSocket close unsubscribes the client. V1 does not add
  `dock/unsubscribe`.

Swift:

- `DockStreamDTO` decodes snapshots, deltas, and heartbeats.
- `DockStreamClient` manages the JSON-RPC/WebSocket stream.
- `DockSessionTable` applies snapshots and deltas mechanically.
- Existing Dock views render projected normalized sessions and host metadata.

## 5.4 Invariants and boundaries

- `notLoaded` is not a valid `dock/*` wire status.
- Valid V1 row statuses are exactly: `running`, `needsInput`,
  `needsApproval`, `idle`, `error`, `dormant`, and `unknown`.
- Codex status mapping is exact at the adapter boundary:

| Codex adapter input | Dock Home wire status | Reason |
| ------------------- | --------------------- | ------ |
| `running` / live running equivalent | `running` | Active work is visible. |
| needs-input equivalent | `needsInput` | User action is needed. |
| needs-approval equivalent | `needsApproval` | Approval action is needed. |
| idle / completed / inactive history equivalent | `idle` | Known non-running row. |
| error / failed equivalent | `error` | Failure is user-visible. |
| `notLoaded` | `dormant` | The provider has history, but the runtime is not loaded; this is not a user-facing product state. |
| unknown / unmapped provider status | `unknown` | Adapter could not classify without lying. |
- `lane` is on the wire as `human` or `agent`.
- `kindLabel` is display-only and not a branching key.
- Host connection, table freshness, and row runtime status are separate fields.
- Raw provider metadata, secrets, loopback URLs, and `dockRelaySource` stay
  relay-side.
- V1 stores last-good state as atomic JSON, not SQLite.
- V1 uses per-host streams and trivial client union; coordinator/federation is
  deferred under the same envelope.
- Dock Home cutover is a clean cutover after proof, not a permanent fallback.

262	`makeSnapshot(...)` then builds rows only from the current refresh outcomes:
263	
264	```swift
265	var summaries: [SessionSummary] = []
266	...
267	for outcome in results {
268	    ...
269	    summaries.append(contentsOf: hostDedupedSummaries)
270	}
271	...
272	for host in hosts where checkingHostIDs.contains(host.id) {
273	    hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: hostViewModel, status: .checking)
274	}
275	...
276	let rows = projector.rows(from: summaries)
277	```
278	
279	The missing piece: there is no "last good rows per host" cache used for a still-checking host. A still-checking host contributes host state only, not stale rows.
280	
281	## Why Home selected goes to zero
282	
283	`CodexDock/State/DockSessionProjection.swift` filters visible rows by selected host:
284	
285	```swift
286	if !options.filters.selectedHostIDs.isEmpty,
287	   !options.filters.selectedHostIDs.contains(row.id.hostID) {
288	    return false
289	}
290	```
291	
292	During a partial refresh:
293	
294	- Amir-M5 rows are in `snapshot.rows`.
295	- Home is only in `snapshot.hostStates` as `.checking`.
296	- Home rows from the previous successful refresh are not carried forward.
297	- If the selected host filter is Home, the visible row list is empty.
298	
299	That exactly matches the observed `Home -> 0 -> Checking -> 200` behavior.
300	
301	## Current paging improvement
302	
303	At `3ed11ad`, active session paging is bounded:
304	
305	```swift
306	public static let activeSessionMaxPages = 1
307	```
308	
309	`DockSessionQuery.activeHuman` and `DockSessionQuery.activeAgents` both use that `maxPages`.
310	
311	`AppServerDockClient.loadSessions(...)` stops after `maxPages`:
312	
313	```swift
314	if let maxPages = query.maxPages, pageCount >= maxPages {
315	    cursor = nil
316	    break
317	}
318	```
319	
320	This prevents the older active-Dock behavior where the app drained every active cursor from Home before finishing. Earlier in this same work session, an app-shaped full cursor drain against Home showed:
321	
322	```text
323	Home human all-pages:
324	  10 pages
325	  958 rows
326	  19324ms
327	
328	Home agents all-pages:
329	  reached page 13
330	  1300 rows
331	  66601ms
332	  then timed out at 90s before completion
333	```
334	
335	That explains why the pre-`3ed11ad` experience was much worse. It does not fully solve the current UI problem because the current one-page Home request can still take about 4 to 6 seconds, and stale Home rows are still dropped while the new Home request is in flight.
336	
337	# Relay Code Path
338	
339	## `thread/list` mostly passes through history rows
340	
341	`scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`:
342	
343	```js
344	async function aggregateThreadList(config, params = {}) {
345	  const historyParams = clampThreadListParams(params);
346	  const history = await readHistoryThreadList(config, historyParams);
347	  const data = Array.isArray(history.data) ? history.data : [];
348	  const summaryCache = threadSummaryCacheForConfig(config);
349	  const dataWithSummaries = summaryCache.decorateRows(data);
350	  summaryCache.warmRows(data);
351	  const liveOverlay = history.liveOverlay || liveStatusCacheForConfig(config).liveOverlay();
352	  return {
353	    ...history,
354	    data: dataWithSummaries,
355	    liveOverlay,
356	  };
357	}
358	```
359	
360	What this means:
361	
362	- The relay asks the raw history app-server for `thread/list`.
363	- It decorates row summaries.
364	- It warms summaries in the background.
365	- It attaches `liveOverlay`.
366	- It does not replace row status with live status.
367	- It does not insert loaded live rows into the list.
368	- It does not keep a cached stable host snapshot for the client.
369	
370	## Live discovery is separate
371	
372	`scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` discovers live loopback app-server processes:
373	
374	```js
375	const endpoints = discoverLoopbackEndpoints()
376	  .filter((endpoint) => !excludedURLs.has(canonicalURLString(endpoint.url)));
377	```
378	
379	It then calls:
380	
381	```js
382	thread/loaded/list
383	thread/read
384	```
385	
386	against those live endpoints and builds a live status cache.
387	
388	The important Home result was:
389	
390	```text
391	Home liveStatus.endpoints: 0
392	Home liveStatus.rows: 0
393	```
394	
395	The important Amir-M5 result was:
396	
397	```text
398	Amir-M5 liveStatus.endpoints: 2
399	Amir-M5 liveStatus.rows: 10
400	```
401	
402	If Home is expected to have live Codex sessions, the next investigation should ask why the relay sees zero non-history loopback app-server processes on Home. The relay's discovery regex only sees process lines shaped like:
403	
404	```text
405	codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:<port>
406	```
407	
408	If Home's active sessions are launched under a different command shape, different user, container, service manager, or socket shape, this discovery path will miss them.
409	
410	## Current relay tests protect "do not merge live status into list"
411	
412	`scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` has a test named:
413	
414	```text
415	relay thread/list keeps history status while focused detail can still route live
416	```
417	
418	The test sets up:
419	
420	- live row status: `active`
421	- history row status: `notLoaded`
422	
423	Then it asserts the list row still says:
424	
425	```js
426	assert.equal(rows[0].status.type, "notLoaded");
427	```
428	
429	Plain meaning: the relay behavior that makes the Dock list mostly `Not loaded` is not accidental in the current codebase. It is an intentional contract today. The relay can route detail calls to the live owner, but the list remains history-first.
430	
431	# Raw Codex App-Server Code Path
432	
433	The upstream Codex app-server source confirms that `notLoaded` is a real state with a narrow meaning.
434	
435	`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/README.md`:
436	
437	```text
438	thread/list ... Each returned thread includes status (ThreadStatus), defaulting to notLoaded when the thread is not currently loaded.
439	```
440	
441	The same README says:
442	
443	```text
444	thread/loaded/list - list the thread ids currently loaded in memory.
445	```
446	
447	`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs`:
448	
449	```rust
450	status: ThreadStatus::NotLoaded,
451	```
452	
453	is the default status assigned when a stored thread is converted into a `Thread`.
454	
455	Then `thread/list` asks the thread watch manager for loaded statuses:
456	
457	```rust
458	let statuses = self
459	    .thread_watch_manager
460	    .loaded_statuses_for_threads(status_ids)
461	    .await;
462	...
463	if let Some(status) = statuses.get(&thread.id) {
464	    thread.status = status.clone();
465	}
466	```
467	
468	`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs`:
469	
470	```rust
471	fn loaded_status_for_thread(&self, thread_id: &str) -> ThreadStatus {
472	    self.status_for(thread_id)
473	        .unwrap_or(ThreadStatus::NotLoaded)
474	}
475	```
476	
477	and:
478	
479	```rust
480	fn loaded_thread_status(runtime: &RuntimeFacts) -> ThreadStatus {
481	    if !runtime.is_loaded {
482	        return ThreadStatus::NotLoaded;
483	    }
484	    ...
485	}
486	```
487	
488	Plain meaning: upstream `notLoaded` does not mean "this row is missing basic list data." It means "this thread is not currently loaded in this app-server process's runtime memory."
489	
490	# Root Cause
491	
492	## Root cause 1: destructive partial snapshots
493	
494	The Home zero-row behavior is a client state-management bug.
495	
496	The Dock should treat a refresh as "new data is being fetched for a host." Instead, it treats a still-checking host as "this host currently contributes no rows." That is why a Home filter can collapse to zero even though the app had good Home rows from the previous refresh.
497	
498	This is exposed by Home because Home is slower. Amir-M5 is fast enough that its partial period is tiny from the user's point of view.
499	
500	## Root cause 2: `Not loaded` is technically true but product-hostile as a primary row badge
501	
502	The upstream meaning is precise: the thread exists in history, but it is not currently loaded in a runtime owner.
503	
504	For Dock, that status is not very useful as the dominant row state because most history rows will naturally be `notLoaded`. The row still has useful data:
505	
506	- title or preview
507	- cwd/repository
508	- branch
509	- last activity
510	- source type
511	- host
512	
513	So the row is not "not loaded" in the way a user reads that phrase. It is only "runtime status not loaded."
514	
515	## Root cause 3: the relay leaves too much list assembly burden on the client
516	
517	The relay currently gives the client:
518	
519	- history pages from `thread/list`
520	- a separate `liveOverlay`
521	- live routing for detail operations
522	
523	It does not give the client:
524	
525	- a stable per-host Dock snapshot
526	- a stale-while-refresh contract
527	- merged live statuses for list rows
528	- a server-side answer to "show me the current Dock list for this host"
529	
530	So the client is forced to fan out and rebuild the Dock view from lower-level pieces. That is workable for a fast single host. It is brittle when one host is slower and the UI needs stable filtered views.
531	
532	## Root cause 4: Home has no discovered live rows
533	
534	Home's live status cache reported:
535	
536	```text
537	endpoints: 0
538	rows: 0
539	```
540	
541	That means Home cannot currently upgrade list status from live app-server owners through the relay's live discovery path. This may be expected if Home has no live Codex sessions. If Home does have live sessions, this is a separate relay discovery problem.
542	
543	# What Is Not The Root Cause
544	
545	## Not raw connectivity
546	
547	Both relays responded to `/statusz`. Both relays served `thread/list`. Simulator logs repeatedly recovered to:
548	
549	```text
550	Online message=2 hosts online
551	```
552	
553	## Not overlapping refreshes
554	
555	The refresh loop awaits each refresh, then sleeps 5 seconds. There is no evidence that the app is starting a new Dock refresh before the previous one completes in normal foreground operation.
556	
557	## Not a Swift string-only bug
558	
559	The Swift mapper maps upstream `notLoaded` to the Dock row status:
560	
561	```swift
562	case .notLoaded:
563	    return .notLoaded
564	```
565	
566	The row projector then displays:
567	
568	```swift
569	case .notLoaded:
570	    return .notLoaded
571	```
572	
573	The label is confusing, but the data starts upstream.
574	
575	## Not only the old Home checkout
576	
577	Earlier, Home was running old code and that was a real confounder. Current evidence after syncing Home to `3ed11ad` still shows:
578	
579	- Home requests are much slower than Amir-M5.
580	- Home rows disappear during partial refresh.
581	- all current list rows return `notLoaded`.
582	
583	# UX Meaning
584	
585	The UI should distinguish these concepts:
586	
587	```text
588	Host reachability:
589	  Is the host online?
590	
591	Host refresh state:
592	  Are we refreshing this host right now?
593	
594	Row runtime status:
595	  Is this thread currently loaded/running/idle in a live app-server?
596	
597	Row list availability:
598	  Do we have enough data to show the row in the Dock list?
599	```
600	
601	Today those concepts are collapsed in the user's experience:
602	
603	- A refreshing host looks like it temporarily has no rows.
604	- A history row whose runtime owner is not loaded looks like the row itself is "not loaded."
605	- A slow host looks unstable even when it is online.
606	
607	# Candidate Fixes For Discussion Only
608	
609	No fix was applied in this investigation pass.
610	
611	## Option A: client stale-while-refresh per host
612	
613	Keep each host's last successful rows while a new refresh for that host is in flight.
614	
615	During refresh:
616	
617	```text
618	Home: 200 sessions, refreshing
619	Rows: still visible from last successful Home snapshot
620	```
621	
622	When Home finishes:
623	
624	```text
625	Home: 200 sessions
626	Rows: replaced with fresh Home rows
627	```
628	
629	This directly fixes the zero-row flicker. It is probably the smallest product-correct fix for the current symptom.
630	
631	Primary simulator test requirement:
632	
633	- Configure two hosts.
634	- Make one host slow enough to finish after the other.
635	- Select/filter the slow host after an initial successful load.
636	- Trigger refresh.
637	- Verify the slow host keeps its previous rows while its host state indicates refresh/checking.
638	
639	If current simulator hooks cannot force a slow host, add hooks. This should not rely on unit tests as the primary proof.
640	
641	## Option B: split `checking` from `refreshing`
642	
643	Use `checking` for first load or unknown host state only.
644	
645	Use `refreshing` when the host already has a last-good snapshot.
646	
647	This makes the UI language match reality:
648	
649	```text
650	First load:
651	  Home: Checking
652	  Rows: none yet
653	
654	Later refresh:
655	  Home: Refreshing
656	  Rows: retained
657	```
658	
659	This is strongly related to Option A and may be part of the same client fix.
660	
661	## Option C: relay-level Dock snapshot endpoint
662	
663	Add a relay-owned endpoint shaped for the Dock, for example:
664	
665	```text
666	dock/snapshot
667	```
668	
669	The relay would own:
670	
671	- history paging policy
672	- status merge policy
673	- stale-while-refresh behavior
674	- per-host caching
675	- live status integration
676	
677	The client would ask for the current host snapshot instead of rebuilding everything from lower-level history and live endpoints.
678	
679	This is a bigger architectural fix, but it fits the product direction better if the relay is meant to simplify the phone client.
680	
681	Primary simulator test requirement:
682	
683	- App connected to real relay.
684	- Relay snapshot refresh in progress.
685	- Host-filtered UI remains stable.
686	- Offline/error states still render correctly when the host path is unavailable.
687	
688	## Option D: relay merges live status into `thread/list` rows
689	
690	The relay already knows about live rows on Amir-M5. It could replace `notLoaded` status on matching list rows when a live row exists.
691	
692	This would change an existing protected behavior. `scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` currently asserts that history status wins for `thread/list`, even when live detail routing is available.
693	
694	So this is not a trivial cleanup. It is a product/API contract decision.
695	
696	## Option E: reduce `Not loaded` prominence
697	
698	Even if upstream keeps `notLoaded`, the Dock row badge does not have to present it as the main row status.
699	
700	Possible UX interpretations:
701	
702	- Show no status badge for `notLoaded` history rows.
703	- Show `History` instead of `Not loaded`.
704	- Show runtime statuses only when they are meaningful: `Running`, `Needs input`, `Error`, maybe `Idle`.
705	- Move `Not loaded` into a debug/detail field or filter, not the default row badge.
706	
707	This does not fix the Home zero-row flicker, but it addresses the "everything says Not loaded" product problem.
708	
709	## Option F: investigate Home live discovery
710	
711	If Home is expected to have active Codex sessions, inspect why the relay sees:
712	
713	```text
714	liveStatus.endpoints: 0
715	liveStatus.rows: 0
716	```
717	
718	The likely checks:
719	
720	```bash
721	ps -axo pid,command | rg 'codex app-server --listen ws://127\\.0\\.0\\.1:'
722	```
723	
724	and whether Home sessions are launched:
725	
726	- under the same user as the relay
727	- with a different command shape
728	- in a container namespace
729	- through a non-loopback socket
730	- without `codex app-server --listen ...`
731	
732	This is separate from the client stale-row bug. Fixing live discovery would make statuses more useful, but it would not by itself stop stale Home rows from disappearing during refresh.
733	
734	# Recommended Direction
735	
736	The clean product path is probably:
737	
738	1. Fix the client to retain last-good host rows during refresh.
739	2. Rename the refresh state so first load is `Checking` and later refresh is visibly different.
740	3. Decide whether `Not loaded` should remain a visible row status at all.
741	4. Separately decide whether the relay should provide a Dock-shaped snapshot or merge live statuses into list rows.
742	5. Investigate Home live discovery only if Home should have active live sessions right now.
743	
744	The first fix should be simulator-proven. A unit test can cover the state reducer behavior, but it should not be treated as completion evidence. The important proof is the visible simulator behavior with a slow host selected.

# TL;DR

There are two separate problems that look like one bad UI state.

1. The Home row count flaps because the client rebuilds each refresh from only the hosts that have completed in that refresh. Amir-M5 finishes quickly, so its rows stay visible. Home is slower, so when Home is selected, the current refresh temporarily has zero Home rows and a `Checking` host state until Home's new request finishes.

2. `Not loaded` is coming from the upstream app-server data. Codex app-server intentionally returns `status: { "type": "notLoaded" }` for stored history rows that are not currently loaded in memory. The relay currently does not merge live status into `thread/list` rows; it only attaches a `liveOverlay`. So the app is not inventing `Not loaded`, but it is presenting an upstream implementation detail too loudly.

Home is synced to the same client repo commit as this Mac, `3ed11ad`. The current Home relay is reachable and healthy. The old code and old Home checkout were confounders earlier, but they are not the whole explanation for the current UI behavior.

# Investigation Bounds

This pass did not make source-code changes. It used direct JSON-RPC relay probes, simulator unified logs, repo source reads, and Codex app-server source reads.

No screenshots were used. No simulator UI automation was used. This avoids stealing macOS focus while still proving the timing and data path.

Current code version:

- Local repo: `codex-dock-agents-tab-live-counts`
- Local HEAD: `3ed11ad Bound active Dock session paging`
- Local worktree before writing this doc: clean
- Home repo HEAD: `3ed11ad`
- Home worktree status from `git status --short --untracked-files=all`: clean output

# User-Visible Symptom

When the Dock view is filtered or focused on Home, it can show this loop:

```text
Home: 200 sessions
Home: Checking
Home: 0 shown
Home: 200 sessions
```

Amir-M5 usually looks stable because it finishes first. If the selected host is Amir-M5, the partial snapshot already contains Amir-M5 rows, so there is no visible drop to zero for that selected host.

# Ground Truth Summary

## Current relay health

Both relays were online at the time of the direct probe.

```text

  httpStatus: 200
  ok: true
  host.id: Amir-M5
  history.lastHealth.status: up
  liveStatus.overlayState: ready
  liveStatus.endpoints: 2
  liveStatus.rows: 10
  history pool pending: 0

Home statusz:
  httpStatus: 200
  ok: true
  host.id: home
  history.lastHealth.status: up
  liveStatus.overlayState: ready
  liveStatus.endpoints: 0
  liveStatus.rows: 0
  history pool pending: 3
```

Home's `lastClientFacingError` at the time of the probe was:

```text
at: 2026-05-29T19:16:08.886Z
subsystem: history
method: thread/list
code: ECONNREFUSED
retryable: true
message: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4500
```

That error lines up with the earlier service restart. The current probe after that error succeeded.

## Current list-call timing and status distribution

Direct JSON-RPC probe at `2026-05-29T19:30:36.358Z`:

```text

  durationMs: 484
  rows: 100
  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=2, rows=10
  nextCursorPresent: true

Amir-M5 activeAgents:
  durationMs: 159
  rows: 100
  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=2, rows=10
  nextCursorPresent: true

Home activeHuman:
  durationMs: 5978
```

## Refresh loop

- `runDockRefreshLoop()` performs the first `await dockStore.load()`.

- Then it performs `await dockStore.refresh()`.

`CodexDock/Configuration/CodexDockConstants.swift`:

```swift

```

Plain meaning: the app waits for a refresh to finish, waits 5 more seconds, then starts the next refresh.

## Partial host load

`CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift` is the main cause of the Home zero-row flicker.

The load starts with a fresh empty outcome list:

```swift
var outcomes: [HostLoadOutcome] = []
var checkingHostIDs = Set(hosts.map(\.id))
```

As each host completes:

```swift
outcomes.append(outcome)
checkingHostIDs.remove(outcome.host.id)
...
if !checkingHostIDs.isEmpty {
    state = .loaded(makeSnapshot(results: outcomes, checkingHostIDs: checkingHostIDs))

```

`makeSnapshot(...)` then builds rows only from the current refresh outcomes:

```swift

...
for outcome in results {
    ...
    summaries.append(contentsOf: hostDedupedSummaries)
}
...
for host in hosts where checkingHostIDs.contains(host.id) {
    hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: hostViewModel, status: .checking)

...
let rows = projector.rows(from: summaries)
```

The missing piece: there is no "last good rows per host" cache used for a still-checking host. A still-checking host contributes host state only, not stale rows.

- Amir-M5 rows are in `snapshot.rows`.
- Home is only in `snapshot.hostStates` as `.checking`.
- Home rows from the previous successful refresh are not carried forward.
- If the selected host filter is Home, the visible row list is empty.

The upstream Codex app-server source confirms that `notLoaded` is a real state with a narrow meaning.


```rust
status: ThreadStatus::NotLoaded,
```

is the default status assigned when a stored thread is converted into a `Thread`.

Then `thread/list` asks the thread watch manager for loaded statuses:

```rust
let statuses = self
    .thread_watch_manager
    .loaded_statuses_for_threads(status_ids)
    .await;
...
if let Some(status) = statuses.get(&thread.id) {
    thread.status = status.clone();

```

`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs`:

```rust
    self.status_for(thread_id)
        .unwrap_or(ThreadStatus::NotLoaded)

```

```rust
    if !runtime.is_loaded {
        return ThreadStatus::NotLoaded;
    }
    ...

```

Plain meaning: upstream `notLoaded` does not mean "this row is missing basic list data." It means "this thread is not currently loaded in this app-server process's runtime memory."

# Root Cause

## Root cause 1: destructive partial snapshots

The Home zero-row behavior is a client state-management bug.

The Dock should treat a refresh as "new data is being fetched for a host." Instead, it treats a still-checking host as "this host currently contributes no rows." That is why a Home filter can collapse to zero even though the app had good Home rows from the previous refresh.

This is exposed by Home because Home is slower. Amir-M5 is fast enough that its partial period is tiny from the user's point of view.

## Root cause 2: `Not loaded` is technically true but product-hostile as a primary row badge

The upstream meaning is precise: the thread exists in history, but it is not currently loaded in a runtime owner.

For Dock, that status is not very useful as the dominant row state because most history rows will naturally be `notLoaded`. The row still has useful data:

- title or preview
- cwd/repository
- branch
- last activity
- source type
- host

So the row is not "not loaded" in the way a user reads that phrase. It is only "runtime status not loaded."

## Root cause 3: the relay leaves too much list assembly burden on the client

The relay currently gives the client:

- history pages from `thread/list`
- a separate `liveOverlay`
- live routing for detail operations

It does not give the client:

- a stable per-host Dock snapshot
- a stale-while-refresh contract
- merged live statuses for list rows
- a server-side answer to "show me the current Dock list for this host"

So the client is forced to fan out and rebuild the Dock view from lower-level pieces. That is workable for a fast single host. It is brittle when one host is slower and the UI needs stable filtered views.

## Root cause 4: Home has no discovered live rows

Home's live status cache reported:

```text
endpoints: 0
rows: 0
```

That means Home cannot currently upgrade list status from live app-server owners through the relay's live discovery path. This may be expected if Home has no live Codex sessions. If Home does have live sessions, this is a separate relay discovery problem.

# What Is Not The Root Cause

## Not raw connectivity

Both relays responded to `/statusz`. Both relays served `thread/list`. Simulator logs repeatedly recovered to:

```text
Online message=2 hosts online
```

## Not overlapping refreshes

The refresh loop awaits each refresh, then sleeps 5 seconds. There is no evidence that the app is starting a new Dock refresh before the previous one completes in normal foreground operation.

## Not a Swift string-only bug

The Swift mapper maps upstream `notLoaded` to the Dock row status:

```swift
case .notLoaded:
    return .notLoaded
```

The row projector then displays:

```swift
case .notLoaded:
    return .notLoaded
```

The label is confusing, but the data starts upstream.

## Not only the old Home checkout

Earlier, Home was running old code and that was a real confounder. Current evidence after syncing Home to `3ed11ad` still shows:

- Home requests are much slower than Amir-M5.
- Home rows disappear during partial refresh.
- all current list rows return `notLoaded`.

# UX Meaning

The UI should distinguish these concepts:

```text
Host reachability:
  Is the host online?

Host refresh state:
  Are we refreshing this host right now?

Row runtime status:
  Is this thread currently loaded/running/idle in a live app-server?

Row list availability:
  Do we have enough data to show the row in the Dock list?
```

Today those concepts are collapsed in the user's experience:

- A refreshing host looks like it temporarily has no rows.
- A history row whose runtime owner is not loaded looks like the row itself is "not loaded."
- A slow host looks unstable even when it is online.

# Candidate Fixes For Discussion Only

No fix was applied in this investigation pass.

## Option A: client stale-while-refresh per host

Keep each host's last successful rows while a new refresh for that host is in flight.

During refresh:

```text
Home: 200 sessions, refreshing
Rows: still visible from last successful Home snapshot
```

When Home finishes:

```text
Home: 200 sessions
Rows: replaced with fresh Home rows
```

This directly fixes the zero-row flicker. It is probably the smallest product-correct fix for the current symptom.

Primary simulator test requirement:

- Configure two hosts.
- Make one host slow enough to finish after the other.
- Select/filter the slow host after an initial successful load.
- Trigger refresh.
- Verify the slow host keeps its previous rows while its host state indicates refresh/checking.

If current simulator hooks cannot force a slow host, add hooks. This should not rely on unit tests as the primary proof.

## Option B: split `checking` from `refreshing`

Use `checking` for first load or unknown host state only.

Use `refreshing` when the host already has a last-good snapshot.

This makes the UI language match reality:

```text
First load:
  Home: Checking
  Rows: none yet

Later refresh:
  Home: Refreshing
  Rows: retained
```

This is strongly related to Option A and may be part of the same client fix.

## Option C: relay-level Dock snapshot endpoint

Add a relay-owned endpoint shaped for the Dock, for example:

```text
dock/snapshot
```

The relay would own:

- history paging policy
- status merge policy
- stale-while-refresh behavior
- per-host caching
- live status integration

The client would ask for the current host snapshot instead of rebuilding everything from lower-level history and live endpoints.

This is a bigger architectural fix, but it fits the product direction better if the relay is meant to simplify the phone client.

Primary simulator test requirement:

- App connected to real relay.
- Relay snapshot refresh in progress.
- Host-filtered UI remains stable.
- Offline/error states still render correctly when the host path is unavailable.

## Option D: relay merges live status into `thread/list` rows

The relay already knows about live rows on Amir-M5. It could replace `notLoaded` status on matching list rows when a live row exists.

This would change an existing protected behavior. `scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` currently asserts that history status wins for `thread/list`, even when live detail routing is available.

So this is not a trivial cleanup. It is a product/API contract decision.

## Option E: reduce `Not loaded` prominence

Even if upstream keeps `notLoaded`, the Dock row badge does not have to present it as the main row status.

Possible UX interpretations:

- Show no status badge for `notLoaded` history rows.
- Show `History` instead of `Not loaded`.
- Show runtime statuses only when they are meaningful: `Running`, `Needs input`, `Error`, maybe `Idle`.
- Move `Not loaded` into a debug/detail field or filter, not the default row badge.

This does not fix the Home zero-row flicker, but it addresses the "everything says Not loaded" product problem.

## Option F: investigate Home live discovery

If Home is expected to have active Codex sessions, inspect why the relay sees:

```text
liveStatus.endpoints: 0
liveStatus.rows: 0
```

The likely checks:

```bash
ps -axo pid,command | rg 'codex app-server --listen ws://127\\.0\\.0\\.1:'
```

and whether Home sessions are launched:

- under the same user as the relay
- with a different command shape
- in a container namespace
- through a non-loopback socket
- without `codex app-server --listen ...`

This is separate from the client stale-row bug. Fixing live discovery would make statuses more useful, but it would not by itself stop stale Home rows from disappearing during refresh.

# Recommended Direction

The clean product path is probably:

1. Fix the client to retain last-good host rows during refresh.
2. Rename the refresh state so first load is `Checking` and later refresh is visibly different.
3. Decide whether `Not loaded` should remain a visible row status at all.
4. Separately decide whether the relay should provide a Dock-shaped snapshot or merge live statuses into list rows.
5. Investigate Home live discovery only if Home should have active live sessions right now.

The first fix should be simulator-proven. A unit test can cover the state reducer behavior, but it should not be treated as completion evidence. The important proof is the visible simulator behavior with a slow host selected.
